source_title: Hero Haughey's 'surreal moment' after Arsenal shock
source_excerpt:
Teenager Haughey scored the winning Fleetwood penalty in the shootout at Highbury
"My phone wouldn't work for two to three hours after the game because there were so many messages, just notifications after notifications."
It was a Tuesday evening like no other for Fleetwood Town defender Conor Haughey after he scored the winning penalty that helped the League Two side dump Premier League champions Arsenal out of the Carabao Cup in a 5-3 shootout win.
The teenager's emphatic fifth spot-kick in the last-16 tie flew into the top corner to spark a pitch invasion at Highbury Stadium as Fleetwood pulled off one of the biggest shocks in the history of the competition.
Haughey's phone was almost instantly flooded with messages from friends and family back home in Belfast congratulating him on his big moment.
And that was before he hit the headlines again when his excitement spilled over in his post-match interview.
The sweary video of his reflections, like the spot-kick itself, has gained significant traction on social media.
"There was too many emotions going on, it was just wild. I'm from the New Lodge, I've been brought up like that and it just came out," Haughey told BBC Sport NI's Thomas Kane when asked about the interview that had gone viral.
"It's been like a dream. I woke up this morning and was like 'this actually is real'. It's unbelievable and a surreal moment.
"We knew going into the game we weren't going to be overawed, we went in with a gameplan and stuck to it and got the victory, so into the next round."

Haughey became the youngest player in Glentoran history when he made his debut as a 15-year-old against Lisburn Distillery in September 2022 before moving to Fleetwood in the summer of 2023.
A Northern Ireland Under-21 international, the centre-back volunteered to take the penalty in the shootout after Viktor Gyokeres had cancelled out Aaron Loupalo-Bi's opener.
On a night in which NI senior boss Michael O'Neill was in the stands to watch promising forward Ceadach O'Neill mark his first Arsenal start with an assist, it was his former JD Academy room-mate Haughey who grabbed all the headlines.
He was selected as the fifth taker and, after Fleetwood goalkeeper Jay Lynch saved a tame effort from Bruno Guimaraes, stepped up to seal the famous win before running over to greet friends and family who had come over from Belfast for the game and joined in the mass pitch invasion.
"We had the first four [takers] and they [the coaches] were like 'anyone else?' and I said 'yeah'," he explained.
"I trust myself to hit one and luckily I went fifth. Lynchy took all the pressure off me with the save. I was a bit nervous when they (Arsenal) were hitting knowing I was going fifth.
"I put the ball down, knew where I was going and stuck it there and ran over to all my mates in the corner and went mad. They were the first people on the pitch. I knew when I put the ball down and hit it I'd run straight over to them."
Fleetwood sit 84 places below the Gunners in the football pyramid and speaking not even 24 hours after the biggest evening of his fledgling career, Haughey said the magnitude of the victory has not fully sunk in.
"It's not really hit me yet. I'm here playing Fifa and some of the Arsenal players are in my team. It's just mad. I'm sitting as if nothing has happened, as if it's a normal rest day," he added.
"It's history for the fans and it's just as big a thing for us, beating the [Premier League] champions. They probably have the same buzz I had putting the ball in the back of the net. It was a great feeling."
Haughey said he will be a "bit giddy" when the quarter-final draw is made following Chelsea's game against Liverpool on Wednesday night.
The 19-year-old was quick to answer who he would like to face next at Highbury Stadium as the club look to continue their stunning cup run.
